file_format: one JSON document: a list of entry objects separated by commas (or {"entries": [...]}); bare objects one after another (JSON Lines) are refused; at most 500 entries

meaning.rejected_alternatives: what was considered and not chosen ('none' is an answer, empty is not)

gap.title_convention: <Section>: no evidence yet — the form that marks a PRODUCT or TECH section as explained (need_gap)

values.text: every field is text, except sources and the list fields below

lists.rejected_alternatives: text, or a list of texts (written joined with '; ')

values.title: one line, at most 200 characters, without '**' or '|'
values.over_a_limit: refused, never cut: split the entry
values.never: an HTML comment marker (<!--, -->) in any field

sources.<path>, <path>#heading, <path>:line or <: a tracked file of a repo this brain owns
sources.<repo>:<path>: the same, when the brain owns several repos
sources.file:<absolute path>: an existing, non-secret file (a document the person gave)
sources.user: the person's own answer (the only source that is not outside content)

knowledge_standard: Keep a unit only if all three hold: it is useful in another task; a capable person who was not here would go wrong or waste time without it; you can point to its evidence.

Write each unit as situation (applicability: a recognisable trigger, not "when developing"), judgment (what; how for a process), reason (why; for a decision also rejected_alternatives) and evidence. It must stand on its own for a reader who was not here: no "above", "this" or "plan A".
The state of the moment (not pushed, needs a build, not verified yet, a count that will change) is not knowledge and is not written into any unit.
What one look at the code or the data answers (a signature, a schema, a constant's value, a file's layout) is no lesson.
A problem still open is a gap, never a lesson.
Commit hashes, run ids, version numbers of a document and approval dates are evidence, not knowledge: they stay out of a unit's text.

refusals.shape: a field, type, section or length, or the file's format: fix the entries file and run bootstrap-apply again
refusals.evidence: a source that points at nothing this brain may cite: cite a real one, or drop the claim
refusals.doc: the doc already holds the person's own writing: nothing was added; show them the entry and ask (never edit the entries file for it)
refusals.state: the brain is not setting up: bootstrap writes only a newborn brain
